birth.stop: Charlestown, Nevis: the birth without a marriage
birth.date_confidence: The year is genuinely disputed and is not settled here. A St. Croix probate document of 1768 gives his age as 13, which most modern scholars read as 1755; Hamilton himself claimed 1757 and never corrected it. The day, 11 January, is the traditional one. Coordinates are the birthplace site, now the Museum of Nevis History.

stops.stop: Christiansted, the counting house of Beekman and Cruger

stops.stop: Weehawken, Philip
stops.date_confidence: Dates attested: wounded 23 November, died 24 November 1801. The site is disputed and is not resolved here. Chernow and Wikipedia say Weehawken; Gilder Lehrman's Hamilton Education Program and PBS American Experience say Paulus Hook, present-day Jersey City, several miles away. The pool's claim that Philip died on the same ground as his father is unsupported and is dropped.

stops.stop: Weehawken, the ledge under the Palisades
stops.date_confidence: Date attested. Coordinate corrected twice over: the geography lens gave 40.7645, -74.0134, about 800 m south-southeast and off the Palisades ledge, and the afterlife lens gave 40.7698, -74.0113, which at that latitude is in the Hudson. HMDB marker 7334 for the duelling ground at Hamilton Avenue and Boulevard East reads 40 deg 46.2 min N, 74 deg 1.032 min W. Whether Hamilton fired wide deliberately is disputed and is left open.

stops.stop: Trinity Churchyard, the pyramid
stops.date_confidence: Burial date attested. The Bayard house on Jane Street, where he died on 12 July, is folded into this stop because the exact site is a reconstruction from period accounts, at c. 40.7359, -74.0075. The monument is not dated here: Trinity's Corporation put up a marker soon after the burial, but the surviving pyramid-topped marble is attributed to a later erection associated with the Society of the Cincinnati.

stops.stop: The Treasury, the face that stays on the note
stops.date_confidence: Corrected by ten months. The pool dated the reversal 18 June 2015, one day after the redesign announcement of 17 June 2015; in fact Lew announced the reversal on 20 April 2016, together with Tubman on the front of the twenty and the suffrage march on the ten's reverse.
